instructions.content: Use design-debate for a decision not yet written as a plan file. If a plan file already exists, use plan-review instead.
Do not use design-debate when the question needs narrowing before it is even debatable -- use socratic-method first.
Avoid manufacturing debate when there is only one reasonable answer.
State the decision precisely as a yes/no or A-vs-B choice, not a vague topic, before doing anything else.

Unless hard numbers are already in hand, always investigate current scale, consumers, and blast radius before assigning debate positions -- an ungrounded debate produces confident conclusions built on guessed facts.
Compose one identical brief (decision, grounding facts, candidate designs) for every reviewer so differing conclusions come from role, not from unequal information.
Never assign all reviewers a balanced or neutral framing -- neutral reviewers converge toward consensus that reads as validation but is really unopposed agreement.
Prefer two genuinely opposing roles (Advocate, Skeptic) as the minimum, and always add a Migration/Risk role when the change touches multiple files or downstream consumers.
By default use diverse models across reviewers to catch different blind spots; a single model is acceptable for lower-stakes debates.
Never spawn reviewers sequentially -- spawn all of them in a single message so independent reviews run in parallel instead of tripling wall-clock time.
Synthesize a verdict that names which argument holds up under the others' scrutiny and renders an actual recommendation: proceed, do_not_proceed_for_now, or proceed_with_modification.
Never present raw reviewer output as the final answer -- an unsynthesized list of opinions pushes the decision back onto the user instead of resolving it.
Never let a do_not_proceed_for_now verdict omit a revisit trigger -- a concrete, checkable condition, never 'revisit later' -- or it silently becomes 'never' by default.
Run scripts/validate-debate-verdict.sh against the verdict file to confirm it conforms to the debate-verdict schema before it ships or gets persisted.
Always persist the outcome and always ask explicitly before doing so -- never decide silently, and never skip recording just because the main question got resolved in chat.

Choose the artifact by the verdict: proceed or proceed_with_modification becomes a context-file finding; do_not_proceed_for_now becomes a context-file KNOWN_ISSUE with the revisit trigger as its fix condition.

The same recording rule applies to any individual role's surfaced concern, not just the overall verdict -- a separate concrete gap raised by one role (commonly Migration/Risk) is its own known-issue even under an otherwise proceed verdict.
If the verdict reveals a binding architectural decision, use adr-capture in addition to the finding or known-issue.
If the verdict is proceed, hand off to plan-create using the debate's grounding facts and chosen design as input rather than re-deriving them from scratch.
The value of the debate is real disagreement, not the appearance of thoroughness -- a well-run debate can end in 'no' and that is success, not a failure to reach consensus.
